newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait parliament postpones budget approval.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait parliament postpones budget approval.

text.p: A Kuwaiti parliamentary committee has postponed approval of the Gulf Arab state's 1997/98 draft budget, objecting to its raising of fees, the official Kuwait News Agency said on Wednesday.

"The parliament's finance and economics affairs committee postponed in its meeting today (Wednesday) approval of the state's budget for the next fiscal year 1997/98 (July-June) for its inclusion of raising of fees on citizens," KUNA said.
It said the decision to postpone approval of the budget came because of a projected rise of 200 million dinars ($666 million) in non-oil revenues derived from an increase in fees on citizens.
KUNA did not specify what the disputed fees would be levied for.
By law, the government is not allowed to raise charges on public services without parliament approval.
Kuwaitis enjoy a cradle-to-grave welfare system that offers free education and health and heavily subsidises state services such as electricity and water.
Kuwaiti officials are said to be considering increasing charges on some state services.
The Kuwait government is proposing a 4.37 billion dinar budget for fiscal 1997/98 with a net deficit of 1.17 billion dinars.

The draft budget puts expenditure at 4.37 billion dinars in addition to a 320 million dinar deposit in a fund for future generations, making the gross projected deficit for the next fiscal year 1.49 billion dinars.
The budget proposal, which also has to be approved by the head of state before it becomes law, puts oil revenue at 2.56 billion dinars, almost unchanged from the previous year.
Non-oil revenue was unchanged at 645 million dinars.
